notes.decision: Translated as 3pl perfect 'they gathered them' with 3pl object suffix (Lyc. ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ-ⲟⲩ). Subject is implicit, antecedent presumably on previous page; the 'them' gathered are the cosmic figures whose dwelling place is then established as a prison.

Translated 'transgressed' for the verb describing the Watchers' descent. The lexeme is unusual; possible reflex of ⲡⲱⲃⲥ̄/ⲡⲱⲃϣ̄ with sense 'transgress, defile, fall' fitting the standard Watchers narrative (1 Enoch 6, Mani's Book of Giants). Could alternatively be 'rebel.'

Translated 'depth' as a working hypothesis. The lexeme is opaque; possibly a compound with 3sg.m suffix -ϥ̄, denoting an interior cosmic location ('its depth/interior'). Context (the Watchers' subterranean prison) supports a place-of-confinement reading.
Tentatively rendered 'of their dwellings,' parsing as ⲛ̄- (gen.) + ⲛ-ⲧⲟⲩ- (their) + ⲉⲓⲉⲩⲉ (= ⲏⲩⲉ 'houses,' plural of ⲏⲓ̈?). Could alternatively be a generations/abodes term.

Translated 'twelve' tentatively. The numeral form is unusual; possibly a Lycopolitan reflex of ⲙⲏⲧⲥⲛⲟⲟⲩⲥⲉ '12' with phonetic/orthographic shifts. Twelve fits Manichaean cosmological patterns (twelve aeons, zodiacal twelve). Alternative readings 'thirty-five' or 'thirty-six' (ⲙⲁⲃ '30' + ⲧⲉⲥⲉ?) cannot be excluded. Flag for parallels.

Construed as 'those yet to be begotten, his (offspring) with (the offspring of) one another.' The phrase ⲛⲉϥⲙⲛⲉⲩ ⲉⲣⲏⲩ literally 'his with theirs each-other' renders intermarriage/intra-progeny relations among the giants' descendants. Alternative parsing as 'his fellows with each other' is possible.

Parsed as relative habitual ⲉ-ϣⲁⲩ- + verb-stem (-ⲇ as Lyc. variant of ⲣ̄ 'do/be'?) governing 'a thousand years' (ⲙⲏⲧⲛ̄ⲱⲉ = ⲙⲏⲧ ⲛ̄ ϣⲉ '10 of hundreds = 1000'). Translation: 'those who would (live for) a thousand years.' The thousand-year lifespan of the giants/post-Watchers offspring is a standard Watchers-tradition motif.

Tentatively translated 'this watch ... this watcher who is outside.' Both terms appear to derive from ⲟⲩⲣⲏϩ/ⲟⲩⲣⲱⲱϥ 'watch, vigil, watcher.' In Manichaean cosmological context they likely designate cosmic watch-stations through which the Third Ambassador purifies the light (perhaps the sun and moon ships, or related celestial guards).

Translated 'should distinguish/separate.' The verb is opaque; context (the radiant ones vs the destroyed ones, set 'apart from one another') demands a verb of discrimination/separation. Possibly Lyc. reflex of ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲥ ('raise, distinguish') with eschatological-cosmological force.

Translated 'the radiant ones,' tentatively from a qualitative on the ⲡⲣⲓⲉ/ⲡⲓⲣⲉ root ('shine'); cf. accumulated vocab ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance.' Antithetical with ⲛⲉⲧⲧⲁⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲧ 'the destroyed ones' supports a positive light-attribute. Could alternatively read 'pure' or 'new.'

Translated 'the scandal of the doctrines.' Greek σκανδαλισμός 'cause of stumbling' + Lyc. ⲁⲟⲅⲙⲁ 'doctrine' (in glossary). The phrase names false doctrines as cosmic stumbling-blocks against which Christ is sent.

Translated 'they appointed and brought forth, against them, the blessed Christ.' ⲟⲩⲃⲏⲩ 'against them' refers to ⲧⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲡⲥⲕⲁⲛⲇⲁⲗⲓⲥⲙⲟⲥ — the Father pre-emanates Christ before Error and false doctrines manifest in the cosmos, so that Christ stands ready to confront them.
Tentatively 'they cast/spoke.' Could be ⲁⲩϫⲱ 'they said,' ⲁⲩϫⲟⲟⲩ 'they sent forth,' or ⲁⲩⲭⲱ 'they placed/cast.' Context damaged; precise sense uncertain.
